Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- Failing test: org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64Test.testByteToStringVariations()
  - The test constructs Base64 base64 = new Base64(0); (explicitly disabling chunking) and asserts:
    assertEquals("byteToString static Hello World", "SGVsbG8gV29ybGQ=", Base64.encodeBase64String(b1));
  - This test method includes “variations” (e.g., empty, null, URL-safe), and is intended to verify that the static encodeBase64String produces an unchunked Base64 string, consistent with Base64(0).

- Problematic implementation:
  - Base64.encodeBase64String(byte[]) is currently:
    669-671: public static String encodeBase64String(byte[] binaryData) {
                 return StringUtils.newStringUtf8(encodeBase64(binaryData, true));
             }
    It calls encodeBase64 with isChunked = true.
  - With isChunked = true, the path taken is:
    820-835: encodeBase64(binaryData, true, false, …)
             -> Base64 b64 = isChunked ? new Base64(urlSafe) : new Base64(0, CHUNK_SEPARATOR, urlSafe);
             When true, new Base64(urlSafe) is used.
    255-257: public Base64(boolean urlSafe) { this(MIME_CHUNK_SIZE, CHUNK_SEPARATOR, urlSafe); }
    332-351: Base64(int lineLength, byte[], boolean):
             - lineLength > 0 => chunking enabled (MIME chunk size with CRLF).
  - Therefore, the static method forces MIME-style chunking (line breaks every 76 chars) even when the caller expects a continuous, unchunked string.

- Why the test fails:
  - The test expects Base64.encodeBase64String to return an unchunked Base64 string (e.g., "SGVsbG8gV29ybGQ=" for "Hello World"). While this specific short string would be identical with or without chunking, the test method covers multiple variations and was added to enforce that the static convenience method should not insert line separators.
  - The current implementation hardcodes chunked output via encodeBase64(..., true), which adds line separators for longer inputs, contradicting the test’s expectations and the intended behavior captured in the bug report.

- Conclusion:
  - The root cause is that Base64.encodeBase64String(byte[]) incorrectly requests chunked encoding. It should pass isChunked = false to ensure no line breaks are inserted, aligning the static convenience method with the unchunked behavior expected by the tests.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
